results.reason: Issue 1 cites Agmt §2.2 five-year auto-renewal and computes the 270–240 day window as Oct. 3 – Nov. 2, 2026 against the June 30, 2027 expiry. It explains the five-year lock-in at a higher minimum, which runs to 2032. It recommends a signed amendment or a protective non-renewal notice before the window closes.

Issue 2 cites §5.3's 30-day objection right and the deemed acceptance, with receipt on Aug. 21 and a deadline of about Sept. 20. It states the right has 'almost certainly closed' and recommends confirming with the client whether a timely objection was sent and negotiating concessions.

Issue 5 says §11.1 covers any third-party claim, plainly reaching product-defect claims, and is uncapped. It says Brightmere's §11.2 indemnity is capped and calls the result lopsided. It recommends narrowing §11.1 to Halvorsen's own breach or negligence.

Issue 4 explains that Amend. §3.1 deletes the §12.3(b) recall carve-out, so §9.3 reimbursement is now capped at 12 months' payments. It notes a large recall could exceed that amount and recommends reinstating the carve-out.
Issue 3 identifies Amend. §6 Delaware law and Wilmington forum, the conflict with Agmt §§17.1–17.2 New York law and forum, and precedence under §1.4. It recommends restoring New York law and forum.
The memo states the Notice was delivered on Aug. 21, 2026.
The memo states the Initial Term ends June 30, 2027.
The memo states that under Agmt §1.4 the Amendment outranks the Agreement body.
The document is a memo to the Supervising Partner, and each issue has Where, Why it matters, and Fix sections.
The memo concludes the recall reimbursement is now capped.
The memo acknowledges that the Delaware provisions now govern.
